papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using S
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify cell adhesion-related gene signatures associated with cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors highlight the role of these genes in oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, suggesting potential therapeutic targets to reduce inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity.

papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: crumblr is a new statistical method for analyzing changes in cell type composition from single-cell data across large cohorts. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs, making the analysis fast and flexible. This addresses a key challenge in compositional data analysis for identifying disease- or condition-related shifts in cell frequencies.

papers.title: A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis reveals transcript-level regulation in alternative splicing. With the rapid adoption of long-read sequencing in bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, reliable evaluation of DTU methods under real biological conditions becomes essential. Current evaluation frameworks mainly rely on simulated data, which can introduce bias and may not reflect true regulatory mechanisms. A real-data-driven framework is constructed to evaluate DTU methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. The framework includes two key components
papers.summary: This paper introduces a real-data-driven benchmarking framework for evaluating differential transcript usage (DTU) methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. Unlike prior evaluations that rely mainly on simulated data, this framework uses real biological data to assess method reliability, addressing potential biases in simulation-based benchmarks. It provides a systematic resource for comparing DTU tools across emerging long-read sequencing modalities.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to 1-nitropyrene, a diesel-derived pollutant, causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice, with extravillous trophoblasts identified as a key vulnerable cell type. By integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with the Scissor machine learning algorithm, the authors pinpoint core regulatory targets underlying trophoblast dysfunction.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain, addressing limitations of prior single-cell RNA-seq studies. It reveals cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics across the ~240 circadian neurons and their subtypes. The work provides a more robust molecular characterization of circadian neuron heterogeneity and their responses to light.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing multicollinearity that complicates human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and recovers true biological signals even from highly entangled covariates, enabling counterfactual 'what-if' analyses.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family transcription factors and predicts which of their target genes also oscillate, bypassing the need for costly and time-consuming bioluminescence imaging of each gene. The tool leverages existing expression data to reconstruct oscillation patterns, offering a scalable way to study Notch-driven ultradian rhythms in processes like pancreatic development, muscle stem cell maintenance, and neurogenesis.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper introduces a meta-classifier that arbitrates disagreements between ten gene regulatory network inference methods on an edge-by-edge basis, rather than picking one method or averaging all of them. The gradient-boosted classifier learns from the raw scores each method assigns to candidate regulator-target pairs, allowing method weighting to vary per edge, and the authors also provide a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts.

papers.title: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data to Identify Lactylation-Related Gene Signatures in Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is not only a common complication of liver transplantation and major hepatic surgery but also a critical determinant of postoperative prognosis. Lactate metabolic reprogramming has been observed in HIRI, yet the role of lactate and its related lactylation in the pathogenesis of HIRI remains unclear. To address this, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with multiple bioinformatic approaches. Five single-cell gene set activity scoring methods (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore) were applied to evaluate lactylation activity
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to identify lactylation-related gene signatures associated with hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI), a common complication of liver transplantation and major liver surgery. Using five gene set activity scoring methods and machine learning algorithms, the authors characterize lactylation activity across cell populations and identify candidate gene signatures. The work highlights lactate metabolism and protein lactylation as potentially important mechanisms in HIRI pathogenesis.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data from NSCLC patients to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to predict survival and immunotherapy response. The signature stratifies patients into high- and low-PIS groups with distinct outcomes and immune infiltration patterns, and identifies ADAM12 as a key functional regulator validated in cell lines and mouse models. The work suggests PIS could serve as a biomarker for guiding immunotherapy decisions in NSCLC.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data with ten integrated machine learning algorithms to build an ac4C-related gene prognostic signature (acRGBS) for colon adenocarcinoma. The four-gene signature (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C) stratified patients by prognosis and was linked to immune microenvironment and genomic features, with in vitro experiments validating TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to dissect the ovarian cancer microenvironment, identifying chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight fibroblast-enriched residual disease as a therapeutic vulnerability and provide candidate cell populations for prognostic stratification.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue structure and protein markers, allowing them to map the development of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye using immunohistochemistry and single-cell RNA-seq data. This provides a unified developmental atlas of pigmented ocular tissues, which was previously difficult due to melanin interference.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms across three cancer single-cell RNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells. The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score (BDS) to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, finding that normalization choice affects biological interpretation more than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that computational pipeline decisions can substantially alter downstream biological conclusions in cancer scRNA-seq studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This paper investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbiota and their metabolites migrate to the intervertebral disc microenvironment and contribute to disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify key microbes and molecular mechanisms mediating this cross-kingdom migration, though the abstract does not yet report specific findings.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates publicly available fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify lipidomic features associated with a colorectal cancer-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The analysis suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and the cholesteryl ester CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression trajectory. The findings are computational and hypothesis-generating, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood to identify NETosis-associated gene programs and a stratified pattern of adaptive immune suppression in patients with severe acute pancreatitis. The findings suggest that blood-based transcriptional signatures could help distinguish severe-spectrum disease and highlight neutrophil extracellular trap formation and immune suppression as key mechanisms. This may support early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework designed to handle large-scale scRNA-seq datasets by combining a fast Louvain algorithm for initial cluster generation with a Transformer-based refinement step. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to very large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Single-cell-informed senescence programs underpin a machine-learning prognostic model robustly validated across melanoma cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) shapes tumor evolution and the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet senescence-informed prognostic models for skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a robust senescence-related prognostic signature by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data with systematic machine-learning screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to define senescence-associated programs in skin cutaneous melanoma and uses machine-learning screening to build a prognostic signature. The resulting model is validated across multiple independent melanoma cohorts, suggesting senescence-informed signatures can stratify patient outcomes.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify natural killer (NK) cell-related hub genes in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and builds a two-gene risk model for diagnosis. The authors validate this model as a potential biomarker tool for COPD, highlighting NK cell involvement in disease pathology.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific immune cell state—JAML+ lipid-associated macrophages—that shows high transcriptome-wide association activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche mapping, and machine learning, the authors link genetic susceptibility loci to a pathogenic macrophage program in the diseased liver. The work provides a cell-type-specific framework for understanding how PSC risk genes drive immune-mediated fibrosis.
